incidents.victim: Moldovan government services
incidents.attacker: Unknown — possible foreign state involvement under investigation
incidents.vector: Attackers exploited an unauthenticated, internet-exposed logging service to extract data from interconnected government systems.
incidents.impact: Hackers made roughly 11 million data-access requests and exfiltrated personal, financial, and government records tied to about 750,000 citizens (a third of Moldova's population), forcing officials to disconnect 82 public digital services and 30 government networks.

incidents.victim: PHP-based web servers worldwide, incl. Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS management interfaces
incidents.vector: Unauthenticated remote code execution via two critical PHP core memory-safety flaws (CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619, "PHP2Shell"); technical details leaked ahead of PHP's October 21 emergency patch, giving attackers an early head start.
incidents.impact: CISA confirmed active exploitation and added both CVEs to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog with a federal patch deadline; Palo Alto Networks confirmed successful compromises of internet-facing PAN-OS management interfaces, and researchers estimate more than 22 million exposed, potentially vulnerable PHP instances worldwide.

incidents.victim: U.S. critical infrastructure operators (telecom, energy, water, transportation, government, defense)
incidents.vector: This group continuously builds and dismantles ephemeral chains of compromised SOHO routers, IoT devices, and enterprise edge infrastructure (Fortinet, Cisco, Ivanti, F5, Palo Alto, and others) to maintain covert, hard-to-trace access.
incidents.impact: Lumen's Black Lotus Labs has notified hundreds of victims across telecom, government, defense, water, energy, transportation, maritime, rail, and aviation sectors; the group has exploited zero-days in Versa Director, N-Able N-Central, and Cisco SD-WAN products to preserve long-term access.

incidents.victim: Space/satellite, defense/aerospace, and policy-research organizations
incidents.vector: The group exploited CVE-2026-20127, an authentication-bypass flaw in Cisco SD-WAN Catalyst Controller instances, then deployed a custom malware framework dubbed "KeyDrift" that hooks SSL and socket functions inside legitimate controller processes.
incidents.impact: KeyDrift gave the actor long-term persistence and let it intercept decrypted SD-WAN control-plane traffic to steal IPsec data-plane encryption keys; Cisco Talos assesses the group's infrastructure overlaps with the broader China-linked critical-infrastructure campaign described above.

incidents.victim: Japan Airlines / Japan Transocean Air customers
incidents.vector: Hackers accessed reservation data through Amadeus IT Group, the third-party provider running Japan Airlines' flight reservation, ticketing, and check-in systems.
incidents.impact: 92,000 customers had names, reservation codes, and flight details exposed; about 2,000 also had passport numbers, frequent-flyer numbers, emails, and phone numbers stolen. Flight operations and payment-card data were not affected.

incidents.victim: U.S. Department of Homeland Security employees and contractors
incidents.vector: A hacktivist group calling itself "Department of Peace" said it breached an Okta single sign-on service used by DHS to obtain internal personnel data; Okta states its own systems were not compromised.
incidents.impact: Data on more than 41,000 current and former DHS employees and contractors, including personnel tied to covert operations and the BlueLeaks investigation, was published online by transparency site DDoSecrets.

incidents.victim: U.S. and allied businesses defrauded by DPRK IT-worker schemes
incidents.vector: DPRK IT workers used fraudulent documents, stolen identities, and fabricated personas, aided by cryptocurrency laundering and AI tools, to secure remote employment and then exploited their access.
incidents.impact: Treasury sanctioned 10 individuals and one entity, including Russia-based facilitators and the First Financial and Technical Development Center, for laundering millions of dollars generated through this fraud; some IT workers also deployed malware and exfiltrated proprietary data from employer networks.

incidents.victim: eMudhra Limited (certificate authority) and downstream TLS / code-signing relying parties
incidents.vector: Eight eMudhra intermediate certificate-authority private keys (six TLS, two code-signing) were generated with insufficient cryptographic randomness, allowing the keys to be derived from the public certificates.
incidents.impact: Anyone holding the derived keys could mint trusted TLS certificates to intercept traffic or sign malware to appear legitimate; Microsoft, Apple, and other vendors removed the affected root and intermediate certificates from their trust stores.

incidents.victim: Hospitals, law firms, and businesses in the U.S. and abroad
incidents.vector: As an affiliate of the Nefilim and Hive ransomware-as-a-service operations, Artem Stryzhak gained network access to victim organizations, exfiltrated data, and deployed ransomware demanding cryptocurrency payment.
incidents.impact: The Hive conspiracy alone affected roughly 1,500 victims globally, including hospitals unable to treat or admit patients during the COVID-19 pandemic, causing more than $100 million in combined losses; Stryzhak was sentenced to 70 months in prison, while co-conspirator Volodymyr Tymoshchuk remains a fugitive with an $11 million reward for his capture.

incidents.victim: University of New Mexico Health System
incidents.vector: Ransomware gang BYOD compromised the health system's network, forcing IT to shut down desktops and disconnect devices from hospital Wi-Fi.
incidents.impact: The attack forced a two-hour ambulance diversion, cancellation of outpatient surgeries and appointments at more than 30 clinics, and campus-wide class cancellations; BYOD claims to have compromised 36,000 machines and stolen student, patient, and employee data. A similar cyberattack disrupted University Hospitals in Ohio the same week.

incidents.victim: University of Copenhagen
incidents.vector: Hackers breached a test environment at the university.
incidents.impact: Personal data belonging to more than 525,000 people was stolen.

incidents.victim: Keystone (cryptocurrency hardware wallet maker) and its customers
incidents.vector: A hacker stole Keystone's device authentication key, which is written into every wallet at assembly and cannot be changed.
incidents.impact: Keystone will destroy nearly 19,000 devices and has suspended deliveries, warning the stolen key could be used to build counterfeit wallets with hidden backdoors.

incidents.victim: Organizations across Russia, Belarus, and Kazakhstan
incidents.vector: DataSuckers, a Lapsus/ShinyHunters-style group, conducted hacking and data-extortion operations across the former Soviet space.
incidents.impact: Russian authorities arrested three of the group's four known members, including 19-year-old Denis A. Friedman, who was arraigned in a Moscow court.

incidents.victim: Convertr (e-commerce platform) and its customers' shoppers
incidents.vector: A suspected Brazilian hacking group breached e-commerce platform Convertr via the Plausible open-source analytics platform and injected a credit-card skimmer into its analytics script.
incidents.impact: Payment card data from shoppers on affected Convertr-powered storefronts was harvested by the skimmer; the group has run Magecart-style skimming campaigns since 2024.

incidents.victim: Ledger Nano X customers who purchased through reseller CryptoBilis
incidents.vector: A Southeast Asian reseller, CryptoBilis, distributed tampered Ledger Nano X hardware wallets containing a hidden spy chip.
incidents.impact: Ledger told affected customers to discard devices and move funds to new wallet addresses to prevent theft.

incidents.victim: City of Columbia, South Carolina (municipal government)
incidents.vector: Unspecified ransomware intrusion into city government systems.
incidents.impact: Dozens of resident-facing municipal systems were taken offline, with services continuing to be disrupted days after the attack was confirmed.

incidents.victim: Vanden Broele (Belgian government software supplier) and 120+ local authorities
incidents.vector: Hackers breached Vanden Broele's eSignFlow document-signing platform.
incidents.impact: More than 120 Belgian local authorities were affected; the company took systems offline to prevent further abuse.

incidents.victim: Warp (cloud/developer platform) and roughly 1% of its customers
incidents.vector: Intruders used a swarm of AI agents to breach one of Warp's infrastructure suppliers.
incidents.impact: Agent trace and telemetry data belonging to roughly 1% of Warp's customers was stolen.

incidents.victim: ConnectWise Cloud Backup customers (2,250+ Microsoft 365 tenants)
incidents.vector: A China-linked group used compromised ConnectWise Cloud Backup application credentials and an AI-driven penetration-testing framework (ARTEX) to automate sign-in attempts against downstream Microsoft 365 tenants at up to 2,900 attempts per minute.
incidents.impact: Attackers achieved privileged cloud persistence at multiple organizations across manufacturing, aerospace, chemicals, energy, defense, and financial services within hours of initial access; ConnectWise suspended its Cloud Backup, SaaS Security, and Cloud Management services during containment.

incidents.victim: Accenture (federal contractor) / FBI
incidents.vector: ShinyHunters exploited an unpatched Oracle PeopleSoft platform; Accenture, which managed the system, had failed to install available security patches.
incidents.impact: The breach exposed personal and business data of nearly all FBI special agents; the FBI subsequently terminated its contract with Accenture over the failure to secure the breached systems.

incidents.victim: Country-code domain registries for American Samoa (.as), Ghana (.gh), and Sierra Leone (.sl)
incidents.vector: A threat actor hijacked ccTLD registry DNS records, modifying them to pass domain-ownership verification checks and obtain fraudulent HTTPS certificates for specific domains.
incidents.impact: Google said the threat actor used the hijacked certificates to target some of its services as well as other organizations.

incidents.victim: Blast Mail (email service operated by Laxlight)
incidents.vector: Hackers breached Blast Mail, an email service run by Japanese cloud provider Laxlight.
incidents.impact: The company shut down the service on October 21 and has not resumed operations.

incidents.victim: Sourcenext Corp.
incidents.vector: An unidentified third party misused the company's member-information-retrieval API to pull customer records.
incidents.impact: 22,519,960 customer records were compromised, including emails, passwords, names, addresses, phone numbers, dates of birth, and employment information.

incidents.victim: 40+ port authorities, maritime, and global sea-shipping companies
incidents.vector: The n0n ransomware and data-extortion group compromised a maritime IT services provider and pivoted from that access into more than 40 downstream port authority, maritime, and shipping customers.
incidents.impact: All victims were listed on n0n's dark web leak site; roughly half are known customers of CyberLogitec, a South Korean maritime IT platform provider, highlighting concentrated supply-chain risk across the global shipping sector.

incidents.victim: IDCFrontier (Japanese cloud provider) and 495 downstream companies/local governments
incidents.vector: A ransomware attack on cloud provider IDCFrontier disrupted hosted services relied upon by hundreds of downstream customers.
incidents.impact: 495 companies and local governments experienced service disruption as a result of the single-provider compromise, illustrating the systemic risk of concentrated cloud dependencies.

incidents.victim: At least seven South Korean financial institutions
incidents.vector: A suspected Chinese-speaking actor used the AI-powered penetration-testing framework ARTEX, alongside Claude Code, DeepSeek, Grok, and Zhipu AI, to opportunistically probe and compromise multiple financial institutions' systems.
incidents.impact: Personal data belonging to at least 68,000 people was exposed; the attacker's infrastructure also showed preparations for cryptocurrency-wallet theft and mobile-device exploitation beyond the banking campaign.
